From: Dana Lee <dana@merchantly.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary P1/P2 response latency waiver — Merchantly onboarding

Hi Alex,

Quick context: we’re ramping an ingestion cutover this weekend (big spike in API volume + redis warm-up) and our SREs are predicting consistent short-lived routing congestion during the overnight window (00:00–06:00 PT) for ~10–14 days while caches populate.

We’re asking Redwood for a temporary relaxation of the P1/P2 response commitments for that window during the onboarding period: specifically, allow P1 response SLA to be extended from 15 minutes to 30 minutes overnight, and P2 from 2 hours to 4 hours, for a 14-day window starting Aug 23.

We know this is non-standard — we’re prepared to accept credits or a reduced SLA addendum. Our priority is to avoid service interruptions for end-users while caches/resilience mechanisms stabilize. Attaching our traffic forecast and the onboarding plan for visibility.

Attachments: onboarding-traffic-forecast.csv (text/csv), initial-slo-request.pdf (application/pdf)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can approve this temporary change and what guardrails you’d require (monitoring thresholds, rollback triggers, on-call coverage)?

Thanks,
Dana Lee
Head of Platform
Merchantly

Folks — forwarding Merchantly’s ask. TL;DR: they need a 14-day overnight relaxation (P1 15m->30m, P2 2h->4h) during Aug 23–Sep 5 while caches warm and traffic spikes. They’re open to credits.

Quick assessment:
- Risk: elevated token costs + potential increased error notifications. Business risk if we don’t approve: customer might throttle or delay go-live, could harm renewal timing for DL-2026-0931.
- Mitigation we can offer: temporary on-call augmentation (standby shift covering overnight window), stricter automated alert thresholds, and an agreed rollback trigger (error rate > 1.2% sustained over 15m or latency p95 > configured threshold).
- Credit: propose pro-rated usage credit for duration if SLA breach occurs. Finance/legal sign-off required, but we can draft a short amendment.

Questions for you both:
1) Acceptable approval authorities (Marissa: ops approval? Ben: can you confirm discount/credit guardrails)?
2) Can we commit to a two-week standby rotation (extra headcount) from Redwood side starting the night of Aug 23?
3) What runbook and monitoring links should we require from Merchantly before we accept the waiver?

I’ve attached Merchantly’s forecast to this thread. I’d like to get a decision in the next hour if possible so we can give them downtime plan visibility.

— Alex

Thanks for the context, Alex. I’m OK to approve a narrowly scoped, time-bound waiver with strict controls. Conditions I’m putting on the approval:

1) Waiver window: 00:00–06:00 PT daily, Aug 23 00:00 PT — Sep 5 23:59 PT (14 full nights).
2) On-call: Redwood will provide one dedicated overnight standby engineer each night (rotate). Standby must be paged first for P1s during the window and be available to join an incident bridge within 20 minutes.
3) Monitoring: Merchantly must enable the shared telemetry dashboard and attach the alerting policy (link required) before Aug 22 18:00 PT. We’ll monitor p50/p95 latency and error rate; set auto-escalation if error rate > 0.8% sustained for 10 minutes.
4) Rollback triggers: if we hit error rate > 1.2% for 15 minutes OR if latency p95 exceeds 2x baseline for 30 minutes, Redwood will initiate an immediate rollback and re-enable standard SLA.
5) Credits: if we breach P1/P2 during the waiver period, we’ll credit Merchantly on a pro-rated basis (finance to calculate). Ben, please confirm rough credit bands (0.5x / 1x / 2x monthly pro-rate) and route to legal for a short amendment.
6) Documentation: Merchantly must share the cutover runbook and traffic shaping plan in the linked doc; Redwood will publish the post-mortem template we expect to be completed if an incident occurs.

If Ben confirms credit bands, I’ll sign off and Alex can confirm to Merchantly. I want this documented in a short amendment (SLA addendum) and stored in the customer folder.

— Marissa
Director, Support & Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Dana — thanks for the patience. We can approve a narrowly scoped, time-bound waiver with operational guardrails. Summary of the agreement:

- Waiver window: 00:00–06:00 PT daily, Aug 23 — Sep 5 (14 nights).
- P1 SLA during window: 30 minutes; P2 SLA during window: 4 hours.
- Redwood will provide one dedicated overnight standby engineer (rotate) and will be paged first for P1 incidents during the window. Standby will join an incident bridge within 20 minutes.
- Monitoring: please enable the shared telemetry dashboard and add the alerting policy link by Aug 22 18:00 PT. We’ll watch error rate and latency; auto-escalation thresholds are as discussed.
- Rollback: triggers include error rate > 1.2% for 15 minutes or p95 latency > 2x baseline for 30 minutes — in which case we’ll initiate rollback to prior config and re-enable standard SLA.
- Credits: if we breach during the waiver, we’ll apply pro-rated credits. Ben will follow up with exact banding and a short SLA addendum for signatures.

I’ve linked the cutover/runbook doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/merchantly-onboarding-plan and our runbook for the standby team here: https://redwood.app/ops/runbooks/merchantly-oncall.

Please confirm you accept these conditions and confirm the runbook link + telemetry access by Aug 22 18:00 PT so we can lock the waiver. Once you confirm, Ben will route a short amendment for signatures and Marissa will schedule the standby rota.

Best,
